notes.title: Before Exit Gas Station is shaping up! Wishlist now!🚪
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone! 👋[/h1]

We’re super excited to share with you progres regards Before Exit: Gas Station ⛽✨

[img]https://i.imgur.com/uH6j49V.gif[/img]

If you played (and hopefully enjoyed 😉) our first game, you’ll be happy to know your beloved employee is back, this time working the late shift at a lonely little gas station. Your mission? Close everything down for the night. That means sweeping floors, cleaning toilets, restocking shelves, double-checking the workshop, shutting off the fuel dispensers… basically making sure everything is in order before heading home. Sounds simple, right? Well, not if your boss has anything to say about it - he notices every little mistake, and you’re already this close to getting fired…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42863686/c14cd69b99bbabf89daf022e7463c8de87844b72.png[/img]

Like the first game, this one mixes roguelike elements, puzzles, and a chill walking-sim vibe. And for the first time in the series, you can actually step outside your workplace before calling it a day! 🌙

We’re working hard to bring you that same cozy-yet-tense feeling of the original, but with a fresh twist. And here’s a little teaser for the future: we’re developing a multiplayer mode so you can (maybe) survive those closing shifts together! More on that soon 👀


👉 If this sounds like your kind of night shift adventure, it would mean the world to us if you add Before Exit: Gas Station to your [b]Steam Wishlist[/b]. It really helps us out and keeps you in the loop for updates!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3268520/Before_Exit_Gas_Station/

Thanks for all your love and support - you’re the reason we’re able to keep making these quirky little games. 💛

[h3]Stay tuned, and don’t forget to turn off the lights before you leave 😉[/h3]

notes.title: Electrician Simulator VR - Endless update and DLC announcement!

notes.title: Repair Like Never Before! 🛠️
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/c0033e790daab7c01bf2f06c6696c01e9ad98a37.png[/img]

[i][b]Electrician Simulator VR[/b][/i] just got a lot more hands on. With the brand new [b]Workbench Update[/b] players will gain access to entirely new gameplay possibilities that bring a deeper level of interaction precision and immersion to the virtual electrician experience

Up until now players could install and configure devices but repairing broken objects wasn’t part of the job. That changes now.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/4bce5f095a9f14272f72ebe1d1796febfc98c87d.png[/img]

[h2][b]🔧 The Workbench is open for every electrician![/b][/h2]The update introduces a dedicated repair system, allowing players to fix various broken items using a full set of new tools. But that’s not all. The team at Take IT Studio! has also unlocked a new area in the player’s home. A fully functional workshop, complete with a specialized repair bench and immersive surroundings.

In this fresh space, you’ll take on new missions where your task is to restore malfunctioning devices sent to you by none other than your in-game father. A figure known for his strong opinions and even stronger tendency to hoard "stuff that might still work."

From dusty fans and broken clocks to unexpected little gadgets, you'll now be able to disassemble, diagnose, and bring these objects back to life using:

🔧 Screwdraivers for precise disassembly
🔍 Diagnostic tools to find damaged components
⚙️ Replacement parts to swap in working elements
🔬 Soldering tools to reconnect circuits

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/7777250101d432ef0797be6c69597268627ec9f7.png[/img]

[h2][b]📋 Patch Notes – Workbench Update[/b][/h2]
Here’s what’s included in the update:
✅ Added 4 new items to repair and test in the Workbench section.
✅ Fixed an issue where items in the garage wouldn’t reset to their original positions after pressing the "Tidy Up" button.
✅ Fixed a bug that allowed stacking American-style electrical boxes on top of each other.
✅ Fixed an issue where a lamp component was emitting light when it shouldn’t.

[h2][b]Available now![/b] [/h2]The Workbench Update is available as a free patch for all players on SteamVR, Meta Quest, and PlayStation VR2. Whether you're a returning electrician or stepping in for the first time, now is the perfect time to (re)connect.

[url=https://www.takeitstudio.com/discord][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/79aca786b4b40d3a4024324dc54658f88f5cbce9.png[/img][/url]

Stay charged. Stay sharp. Tighten those screws!⚡
[b]Electrician Simulator VR Dev Team[/b]

notes.title: 🔧 The Art of Repair
notes.content:
[h3][b]Hey Electricians! ⚡[/b][/h3][p]We’re back with a big announcement - one that brings fresh tools, new mechanics, and a whole new reason to spend more time in the virtual garage.[/p][p]Let’s talk about something we’ve been working on for last weeks: the [b]Workbench Update[/b], arriving in the upcoming patch for [i][b]Electrician Simulator VR[/b][/i]. This isn’t just a small addition! It’s the beginning of a new layer of gameplay designed to expand your skills as a virtual electrician… and maybe even as a fixer-upper in general.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/781abd2572e3ab3b1b3b2c525d135b603f14c38d.png"][/img][/p][h2][b]🧰 What Is the Workbench?[/b][/h2][p]In this update, we’re introducing a completely new gameplay feature: the repair system. You’ll now be able to fix broken items using a dedicated work area unlocked inside your in-game home. But wait - there’s more:[/p][p]These items won’t come out of nowhere. Your dad (yes, the same one with very strong opinions about how things should be done 😅) will regularly send you objects that he thinks can be saved. Some are practical, some nostalgic, and a few… a little suspicious.[/p][p]To repair them, you'll gain access to a brand-new part of your house - a workshop area with a fully functional repair bench and specialized tools.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]🔩 What Can You Do There?[/b][/h2][p]Repairing items isn’t just about pressing a button - you’ll need to roll up your sleeves and do things properly. Here's a taste of the tools and techniques you’ll be using:[/p][p] 🔧 [b]Disassembly[/b] – Use screwdrivers to carefully take devices apart without damaging them[/p][p]🔍 [b]Component Identification[/b] – Examine and diagnose faulty parts[/p][p]⚙️ [b]Replacement & Rewiring[/b] – Swap out broken elements with functional ones[/p][p]🔬 [b]Soldering[/b] – Repair connections and bring circuits back to life[/p][p]🕹️ [b]Testing & Usage[/b] – In some cases, fixed items can be used elsewhere… even for fun![/p][p]This addition brings a brand-new sense of progression - you're not just installing new things anymore; you're restoring old ones and giving them a second life. It’s the kind of tactile, detailed work that fits perfectly with VR.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]🛠️ Why Does It Matter?[/b][/h2][p]We always wanted [b][i]Electrician Simulator VR[/i][/b] to be more than just "a job sim". With the [b]Workbench[/b], we’re expanding the way you interact with the world - giving you reasons to come back to the house, check for new deliveries, and solve small mechanical mysteries piece by piece.[/p][p]And honestly? It’s just really satisfying to fix something broken and make it work again. Whether it’s a dusty fan, a retro radio, or something you didn’t even know could be saved - that “click” when it powers on again? It hits different.[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3256020/Electrician_Simulator_VR/"][/dynamiclink][/p][h2][b]🗓️ When’s It Coming?[/b][/h2][p]The full patch will go live next week, and we’ll share a complete changelog then - along with more screenshots, bugfixes, and improvements that have been bundled into this release.[/p][p][url=https://discord.gg/GMHvsYJTsE][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/79aca786b4b40d3a4024324dc54658f88f5cbce9.png[/img][/url][/p][p]Let us know in the comments below, or join us on our official channels to share your feedback![/p][p][/p][p][b]Stay charged, stay sharp, and don’t forget to tighten those screws.[/b][/p][p][b]Electrician Simulator VR Dev Team[/b]


[/p]

notes.title: 🔧 Mission Pack #1 is here!
notes.content:
[h1]Hey Electricians! 👷‍♂️[/h1]

We’re moving forward with the second step of the Electrician Simulator VR roadmap, and this time we’re diving into Mission Pack #1!
As the name suggests, this update brings brand-new content to the game - and it's all about expanding your electrician experience with new challenges!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/49e80bc4fda838e603281c70be7988e7159af0cf.png[/img]

At the heart of this patch are three new story-driven missions that will test your skills in fun, creative, and surprising ways. Whether you're rewiring, troubleshooting, or just exploring new interiors, there's plenty of satisfaction waiting in these fresh jobs!

And of course - we’ve also taken time to fix some of the bugs and issues you reported. Thank you for all your feedback and support - the full list of changes and fixes can be found below.

[h2][b]Change log 1.3.0:[/b][/h2]
[h3]⚡ New:[/h3]
[list]
[*] 3 new levels
[*] Added a button in the player's garage to reset the position of all interactive items in the scene (chairs, cups, cabinets, etc.)
[*] Some older objects are now breakable
[/list]
[h3]🛠️ Bug Fixes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Adjusted the pose when holding the clipboard so it no longer completely blocks the dialogue tab arrow when held in the left hand
[*] Fixed an issue where certain SFX did not respect the sound volume settings
[*] Fixed a bug where the tooltip about resetting item positions would not disappear after using the reset function
[*] Fixed a visual bug with cable alignment when connecting to the cable placement tool in some cases
[*] Fixed an issue where cables from two different junction boxes could be connected to the same outlet/light switch
[*] Fixed a bug where the state of darts stuck in the dartboard was not saved
[*] Fixed an issue where the player would not be electrocuted if power was turned on after grabbing a live cable
[*] Fixed a bug in the "New Opening" mission where the objective for installing lamp covers would not count correctly if the lamp was disassembled and reassembled
[*] Fixed an issue where a new cable could be created on a wall without placing any anchor points
[*] Fixed a bug where darts would fall out of the player's hands when grabbing them
[*] Fixed an issue where the position of certain objects was not saved correctly in the "New Opening" level
[/list]This is the next step in our roadmap, and we’re already working on what comes next! A major new update is on the horizon, bringing even more content, features, and surprises to Electrician Simulator VR.

notes.title: The Hum of Wires
notes.content:
[h1][b]Hello Electricians! [/b]👷‍♂️[/h1]

Today, we’re excited to bring you a special announcement that’s perfect for both Electrician Simulator VR fans and lovers of relaxing, atmospheric sounds. Starting now, you can purchase the soundtrack of the game and the game together with the official soundtrack!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/311cae130cc7a727e9fec7a3cfc27470d2813168.png[/img]

So, what makes this soundtrack stand out? It’s not just a collection of tracks—it’s a carefully crafted audio journey that perfectly captures the atmosphere of an electrician’s world. Gentle, pulsing backgrounds, subtle electronic tones. Together, they create a unique sonic landscape that accompanies you not only during repairs in the game but also in real life, when you want to relax or stay focused.

This soundtrack isn’t just music—it’s an immersion tool that helps you dive even deeper into the world of Electrician Simulator VR. Whether you’re planning your next in-game repair (or maybe a real one 😉), or you’re simply looking for a calming background for your evening chill-out session, these sounds will put you in the perfect state of mind.

And for those who love to bring a bit of their favorite games into everyday life, this is the perfect way to keep that immersive feeling going even when you step away from VR. Imagine sipping your coffee while the soft hum of distant transformers plays in the background or reading a book accompanied by the gentle clicks of tools and circuits coming to life. It’s a small but powerful way to stay connected to the calming, focused world of Electrician Simulator VR—anytime, anywhere.

Behind every track is a thoughtful approach to sound design. The compositions were created to subtly reflect the emotions and atmosphere of the game’s key moments—from the peaceful satisfaction of a job well done to the quiet tension of troubleshooting a complex electrical fault. The ambient nature of the soundtrack makes it perfect not only for background listening but also as a companion for moments of creativity, study, or deep concentration.

👉 Starting today, you can grab the game bundled with the ambient soundtrack and take the atmosphere of the electrician’s craft with you wherever you need a bit of peace, focus… and that subtle electric hum in the background.

May the current flow through your game, and your headphones!

notes.title: Wired and Ready!
notes.content:
[h1]Hey Electricians! 👷‍♂️[/h1]

Today marks the beginning of our official [i]post-launch roadmap[/i] for [b]Electrician Simulator VR[/b]!
[b]The Electrical Systems update[/b] — the first milestone on the roadmap you can see below — brings a changed gameplay elements, and fresh challenges for all aspiring electricians. 🌟

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/6527ed42574c5f97b0aee3603ee45a0d34cd0830.png[/img]

[h3]But that's not all![/h3]
As we continue along [i]the roadmap[/i], [i]Mission Pack #1[/i] is coming in [i]May 2025[/i], bringing brand new story-driven jobs and gameplay challenges that will put your newly sharpened skills to the test!

[h2][b]Change log 1.2.0:[/b][/h2]
[h3]⚡ New:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added the option to select the standard/region, which will change the models for outlets, light switches, electrical boxes, etc. Currently available regions: EU and US.
[*] Openable refrigerators.
[*] Rolling sounds added for balls, light bulbs, and billiard balls.
[*] Improved toaster interaction – it can now be turned on by using your hand.
[*] Added the option to choose between smooth and snap crouching (smooth crouching is the default setting).
[*] Added discounts for lampshades in the "New opening" level.
[/list]
[h3]🛠️ Bug Fixes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where purchased objects would fall out if VR was turned off or entered standby mode during gameplay and then turned back on.
[*] Fixed a bug where the expense card was not saving during missions.
[*] Fixed an issue where the challenge in the "The Art of Connectivity" mission would not complete correctly if the lamp was disconnected and reconnected to power.
[*] Fixed a bug where plugs could fall out of the player's hand if teleportation was used as the movement method.
[*] Fixed an issue where, in some cases, an electrical box could be removed from the wall even if cables were still connected to it.
[*] Fixed a bug where resetting the player position would teleport them to the last save point instead of the starting position for the level.
[*] Fixed an issue where certain objects could be placed improperly on the edges of furniture or walls, appearing as if they were floating or not properly mounted.
[*] Fixed a bug where it was possible to duplicate mission rewards if the player loaded an autosave before exiting the level.
[*] Fixed missing sound effects for collisions/interactions on certain objects.
[*] Improved colliders in some scenes to better match object shapes.
[*] Fixed a bug causing player character jumping when walking down stairs with smooth locomotion enabled.
[*] Adjusted collision strength for glass-breaking effects.
[*] Fixed a bug where players could block mission completion in "Plant Lover" if they disconnected the light switch cables shortly after completing the task to turn on all lights.
[*] Improved sitting interactions on couches in the "House Without Light" level – now you don't need to grab the couch to sit down.
[/list]
In the months ahead, you’ll experience new story-driven challenges with [i]Mission Pack #1[/i], get hands-on with repairs through [i]Workbench[/i], and test your skills endlessly in [i]Endless Mode[/i].

We’re just getting started, and there’s a lot more to share — new patch notes, improvements, and surprises are already in the works.

Stay wired, stay grounded, and we'll keep you updated every step of the way! 💡

notes.title: First Major Patch is Here
notes.content:
[h1]Hey Electricians![/h1]

It’s been almost two weeks since the release of [b]Electrician Simulator VR[/b], and we’ve been absolutely blown away by your support, feedback, bug reports, and — most importantly — the passion you've shown for fixing things (and occasionally breaking them too 😅).

As with any launch, the first days brought both excitement and opportunities for improvement. While many of you were able to dive into the experience and enjoy the game, we also heard that some elements — especially the tutorial — needed more attention and clarity. So… we got to work!

Today, we're rolling out our [b]first major post-launch patch[/b], and it’s packed with fixes, improvements, and new features aimed at making your experience smoother, more immersive, and a whole lot more fun.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/ea64083f87e978cd7a2b0f6e9c2e3f6fc6a4443c.png[/img]

[h2]🎓 New and Improved Tutorials[/h2]
[list]
[*] Redesigned Grandfather’s Tutorial (Parts 1 & 2):
The initial tutorials have been completely overhauled to make them clearer, more direct, and easier to follow — giving players a much smoother entry into the game.
[*] New Tutorial for the Nuru Mission:
A dedicated tutorial section has been added to the Nuru mission to guide players more effectively through its unique objectives.
[*] Additional Hints on New Game Start:
Starting a new game now provides better contextual hints to help orient players from the get-go.
[/list]
[h2]📋 UX & Interface Enhancements[/h2]
[list]
[*] Father's Dialog Archive:
You can now access a dedicated tab in the clipboard to revisit everything your dad has said during missions — perfect if you missed something or need a quick recap.
[*] Challenges Preview in the Garage:
If you’ve completed a mission at least once, you’ll now be able to preview the associated challenges directly in the garage.
[*] Stars Earned from Challenges Are Now Visible in the Mission Tab:
The missions screen now shows both the current and maximum number of stars available for challenges — making progress tracking easier and more transparent.
[*] Exit Button Added:
A proper in-game "Exit Game" button is now available from the menu.
[/list]
[h2]🎮 Gameplay & Interaction Improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] Breakable Objects:
12 new environment objects can now be broken — adding more depth and fun to your interactions.
[*] Dedicated Hand Poses for Items:
Various in-game objects now have dedicated hand poses, improving realism and comfort during use.
[*] Teleport Direction Option:
You can now choose the direction you’ll face when teleporting. This setting can be toggled in the options menu.
[i]Note: The previous ability to teleport and rotate using the same hand/controller has been removed for consistency.[/i]
[*] Improved Shop Interaction:
The shop now opens and closes with the same button. The reset position function is now triggered by holding that button instead of tapping.
[/list]
[h2]👷‍♂️ Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where the “Reset to Defaults” button in the options menu didn’t work properly.
[*] Fixed missing physics on several interactive objects.
[*] Fixed missing collision sound effects for certain breakable items.

notes.title: Wired for the Future
notes.content:
[h1]Where do we come from and where are we going? ⚡[/h1]

It’s only been a few days since Electrician Simulator VR launched, and we’re truly grateful for the warm welcome. So many of you have joined our community and shared your thoughts, feedback, and impressions — and we couldn’t be more thankful. Your messages, reviews, and engagement on Discord have helped shape the direction we’re heading, and we’re excited to keep improving the game together with you. ⚡

As we flip the switch on what’s next, it’s time to take a step back and reflect on how far we’ve come — and show you where we’re headed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/bd37f093eeffb67ebc609a9af281c81547823e77.png[/img]

[h2]🔌 Where We Come From?[/h2]

If you've been with us from the start, you probably know that Electrician Simulator VR is much more than just a port of the original Electrician Simulator. It’s a complete rework — not just in terms of interactivity, but in how the entire gameplay experience is delivered in virtual reality.

From precise hand movements to fully immersive interactions, every mission has been redesigned to take full advantage of VR. Plugging in wires, installing outlets, testing systems — it’s no longer point-and-click, it’s hands-on and reactive. We wanted you to feel like you're really doing the job — and maybe even have a laugh when things go sideways. 🔥😄

Of course, it hasn’t been without its challenges. Supporting multiple headsets (including Valve Index), adjusting hand poses, tweaking sensitivity, and improving clarity in tutorials — these are just a few of the things we’re actively working on right now. The next update is right around the corner, and yes, we’re just getting started.

[h2]Changes Coming in Next Week's Patch[/h2]
[list]
[*] HTC Vive (1st gen) support – will be released as a hotfix. Support was tricky due to the limited number of inputs on the controllers, but the control scheme was reworked to ensure smooth gameplay. It took quite a bit of effort!
[*] Refreshed tutorials – the previous ones felt a bit clunky and required too much guesswork. All tutorials have been rebuilt from scratch for a smoother and more intuitive learning experience.
[*] Input and UI improvements – better interactions for opening/closing the shop, along with more convenient navigation within the clipboard.
[*] Access to previous dad voicelines – it's now possible to review what the father character said via the clipboard, in case anything was missed or forgotten.
[*] New poses, improved SFX, minor bug fixes, and other small polish updates.
[/list]
[h2]🗺️ Where We're Going — The Roadmap[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/ff1319c998fcb4b6248dd95fa367a83ccad16ced.png[/img]

[b]⚡ April 2025 – Electrical Systems Update[/b]
This update will bring region-specific electrical standards into the game—not as something players must adapt to during missions, but as an option they can freely choose. You’ll be able to switch between different systems (such as European or American) directly from the settings, allowing you to play using the electrical standards that interest you the most. It adds flexibility, variety, and extra immersion without locking players into one specific format.

[b]🔧 May 2025 – Mission Pack #1[/b]
We’re bringing you a fresh batch of missions — VR-specific design in mind. You’ll meet new clients, explore new locations, and take on entirely new challenges. Just like the base game, this pack will combine logic-based tasks with a touch of absurd humor, because in the world of Electrician Simulator, things rarely go 100% according to plan.

[b]🧰 June 2025 – Workbench Update[/b]
It’s time to get even more hands-on! The Workbench Update introduces detailed repair mechanics for small devices and modules. Think of this as your own tiny electronics lab, where you’ll use precision tools to fix damaged gadgets — soldering, testing, replacing components. This will be the update for players who love detail and interaction.

[b]🏡 July 2025 – Mission Pack #2[/b]
Even more variety is coming to the experience — with new scenarios ranging from realistic jobs to unexpected tasks inspired by pop culture. Some of these missions will pay subtle homage to iconic TV shows, adding a fun twist for fans who enjoy spotting references. You'll also notice deeper storytelling, as well as alternative ways to complete objectives, giving you the freedom to approach things your own way.

[b]♾️ September 2025 – Endless Mode[/b]
You asked for replayability — we're delivering it. Endless Mode will let you take on procedurally generated jobs and repairs without the limits of a storyline. This mode is perfect for players who want to jump in, get their hands dirty, and enjoy the core gameplay in bite-sized or extended sessions. It’ll be a great way to keep coming back to the game after completing the main content.

Each update in our roadmap is designed to build on the core experience, offering new layers of gameplay, realism, and fun. Whether you're diving into region-specific installations, helping quirky clients, or mastering intricate repair work at your own workbench — there's something new for everyone. And once you’ve completed all the missions, Endless Mode will be there to keep the wires buzzing.

Is that everything? Maybe... maybe not. Stick around and see what else we might plug in.

[h2]📣 Stay Connected[/h2]
Every step of the way, your feedback is what helps us improve. We’re actively listening — whether it’s technical issues, feature suggestions, or just ideas for silly missions (we’ve got a soft spot for those too).

If you haven’t already, join our community on Discord!

In touch!

notes.title: More Than Just Wires
notes.content:
[h2]Hey there, Electricians! ⚡[/h2]

A game filled with great interactions and mechanics is important, but without personality, it can feel empty and lifeless—just a playground without any real purpose. That’s why in Electrician Simulator VR, we didn’t just focus on the tools and tasks; we made sure the world itself has a distinct character, filled with humor and unexpected moments that keep every mission fresh and engaging.

From bizarre client requests to absolute chaos caused by faulty wiring, we wanted to ensure that your time spent in the game is more than just work—it’s fun, immersive, and sometimes completely ridiculous.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/c041774c46add91ad5282dff18e7ac554085fa52.png[/img]

[b]The Humor Behind the Wires[/b]

Not every game needs a deep and complex story, but that doesn’t mean it should lack personality. Electrician Simulator VR is filled with funny, unexpected moments that make the world feel alive and engaging.

One minute, you’re changing a simple lightbulb for an elderly gentleman who swears he’s tried everything—but somehow, the problem still isn’t fixed. The next, you’re dealing with a full-blown electrical fire—and not just some minor sparks. One wrong move and suddenly, flames are shooting up the walls! Before you can even think about fixing the wiring, you’ll have to put out the fire and make sure nothing else is about to go up in smoke.

And then there are the more unconventional jobs. Sometimes, you’ll be called in to hook up a room filled with computers, because someone’s got a serious need for power—maybe a little too much power. It’s just another day of making sure outlets don’t explode and that your clients don’t accidentally knock out the entire neighborhood’s electricity.

Every mission in Electrician Simulator VR is designed to keep you entertained. Whether you’re rescuing clueless clients from their own bad decisions, tackling bizarre electrical disasters, or just laughing at the sheer absurdity of some requests, there’s always something to make you smile.

We believe that humor and personality make even the simplest jobs feel engaging. The world of Electrician Simulator VR isn’t just about flipping switches and fixing wires—it’s about unexpected twists, ridiculous problems, and the chaotic charm of being the one person who can (hopefully) fix it all.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/843a9c6552dae095cb36ec3888ec3614ef1709e0.jpg[/img]
[b]Interaction & Optimization – The Core of VR Gameplay[/b]

In virtual reality, gameplay mechanics are only as strong as the world supporting them. While interacting with objects is a major focus, if the world feels empty, stiff, or unresponsive, the immersion breaks down. That’s why we put so much effort into ensuring that every tool, every action, and every reaction feels just right.

With VR, interactivity is king. Being able to physically unscrew light fixtures, replace fuses, or wire an entire house from scratch makes every moment feel real and rewarding. But responsiveness and optimization are just as crucial. A poorly optimized VR game can make interactions frustrating, while a well-crafted experience ensures that every action feels natural and intuitive.

From smooth object handling to realistic tool mechanics, we’ve been refining every interaction to ensure a seamless and immersive gameplay experience. Whether it’s using a voltage tester, pulling wires through conduits, or flipping a breaker switch, we want these actions to be as satisfying as they are functional.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/34a4ba0ac46dcbb6cb2c85ed586b11d2b3b78a1b.jpg[/img]
[b]Polishing the Experience[/b]

Of course, building a VR game is a constant process of testing and refinement. We’re always looking for ways to improve the world, mechanics, and humor to make sure that the final product is as polished as possible.

Every mission, from the most basic repairs to the most ridiculous electrical disasters, goes through rigorous testing. Our goal is to eliminate frustrating mechanics, improve performance, and ensure that every moment in the game feels rewarding.

We know that VR is all about immersion, and we want every player to feel like they’re stepping into a real, dynamic world—one that reacts, surprises, and entertains at every turn.

[b]Stay Wired with Us![/b]

We’re incredibly excited about the progress of Electrician Simulator VR, and we can’t wait for you to experience everything we’ve been working on. Whether it’s rewiring a house, fixing a ridiculous electrical mess, or just enjoying the hilarious requests from your clients, we hope you’ll love the world we’ve built.

Make sure to join our community on Discord and follow us on social media to stay updated with the latest news and behind-the-scenes content.

Stay grounded! ⚡
[b]Electrician Simulator VR Dev Team[/b]

notes.title: Rewiring The Classics
notes.content:
[h2]Hey there, Electricians! ⚡[/h2]

By now, you’ve got a good grip on how the game works and the kinds of tasks waiting for you. But let’s flip the switch and talk about the gameplay itself.

[b]Fan Favorites[/b]

We all have that one mission we can’t help but love. Maybe it’s the one with the old guy who called you to replace a light bulb but forgot to mention the real problem was in the wiring—after he’d already swapped the bulb a dozen times. Do you enjoy tracking down sneaky installation errors?

Or maybe you’re more into the hands-on stuff, like moving and replacing appliances, avoiding the big repair jobs altogether. Or are you the type who craves the big challenges, like wiring an entire installation from scratch—a blank wall just waiting for your magic touch?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/1ec74096e14bff78365520bafc10a5a3bbfb7e7f.png[/img]

[b]What’s Changing?[/b]

Don’t worry—all those classic missions you know and love are still here in the VR version. But, as you’d expect, the way you’ll tackle them is completely different. On PC or console, it was all about clicking your way through tasks. But now? You’re stepping into the role, literally.

From unscrewing light bulbs and opening drawers to attaching cables, everything will feel more lifelike. You’ll even be opening boxes with a wallpaper knife or handling fragile items that can break if you’re not careful. You’ve gotta bring your A-game to these tasks!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/42725cb2c02c3c6e0d792a5991502fb34cccdc6c.gif[/img]

[b]Anything New?[/b]

As for missions themselves? For now, we’re sticking with the classics, but here’s the twist: moving them to VR has transformed every mission into a fresh challenge. We’ve reworked them from the ground up to suit the new, immersive experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/10c97b1f58ece89a34432f420c065ed9502e2bbf.gif[/img]

Sure, we’ve spilled a lot of details here, but let’s be honest—nothing compares to experiencing it for yourself. So get hyped for the release of Electrician Simulator VR! And as for the future? Well, who knows what other sparks we’ve got up our sleeves? 😉

notes.title: A Smarter Interface
notes.content:
[h2]Hey there, Electricians! ⚡[/h2]

We all know what an electrician does, but the real question is how they do it. More specifically—what you’ll be able to do in the game and how you’ll interact with the tools of the trade. Today, we’re diving into the nuts and bolts of the new UI elements in Electrician Simulator VR.

[b]Check it Out[/b]

Your mission details are going old-school... sort of. You’ll keep all your tasks and notes on a clipboard that’s always by your side. Need to check what’s next? Just reach for it—it’s like unfastening it from your belt, and boom, your trusty clipboard is in your hands.
But remember, any good electrician knows better than to read while fixing. Keep your focus on one thing at a time, or you might short-circuit your progress!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/6c6a94db174803af866ef458e76e54cdf690e663.png[/img]

[b]Tick Tock, Watch the Clock[/b]

Your smartwatch is leveling up! It’ll still show real-world time (because, hey, someone’s gotta keep track), but now it’s packed with extras.
You’ll get calls from customers right on your wrist, complete with their photo and name. It’ll even monitor your pulse, so if something shocking happens—like, say, a little zap—you’ll know right away. Fingers crossed it never has to send that alert!
While you won’t be able to interact with the watch directly, it’ll always keep you updated on mission progress and other critical info.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/586e9d40c3d44b383cdc9e31cc9c35fc4ebe95a8.gif[/img]

[b]What’s in Store?[/b]

The in-game store has had a bit of a makeover! Forget about physical locations—now the store is fully virtual, and you can pull it up anytime. Just press the menu button on your left controller, and you’re good to go.
Need to buy tools or parts? Point and click with the laser and grab what you need. Selling items? Just place the item in the store’s UI, and it’s gone.
Worried about blowing your budget? Don’t sweat it. During missions, the store will show you how much cash you’ve got for the job. And back at the workshop, you’ll see your total account balance—hopefully growing as you nail those commissions!

[b]Get a Grip[/b]

Your hands are about to become your best friends. When interacting with objects, you’ll see helpful prompts like, “Cables not connected” or hints about what actions are available. You’ll also know which objects are grabbable, as their names will pop up when you hover over them.

These on-hand messages are here to keep the gameplay flowing smoothly and ensure you always know what’s at your fingertips—literally!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/538215caedb34f97c96ca24a20bb8ae4ddafaac5.gif[/img]

That’s all for now, Electricians! We hope these updates have sparked your interest and amped up your excitement for Electrician Simulator VR. Keep your tools ready and your anticipation high—there’s more to come soon. See you in the next devlog!

Stay connected!

notes.title: Electrifying Upgrades
notes.content:
[h2]Hey there, Electricians! ⚡[/h2]

Things are sparking up over here! Right now, we’re fine-tuning all the cool items you’ll be assembling during your jobs, and we’ve gotta say—we’re pretty proud of how they’re shaping up. VR has its own set of challenges when it comes to mechanics, but it also gives us the chance to make the game feel even more real.

And it’s not just about things like opening drawers and cabinets with physics-based interactions (though, yes, we’ve nailed that too). We’re adding big upgrades and tiny details to make sure the game feels alive and intuitive—so your everyday actions, like grabbing or opening stuff, feel natural and fun instead of frustrating.

So, what’s in store for you this time? Let’s flip the switch and take a look.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/4d3a2e338002abaf24a2920a636a2a32c2c1a4bd.png[/img]

[b]Let There Be Light[/b]

Do you enjoy assembling lamps? We’ve got plenty of that lined up, but we’ve added a little extra spark to keep it interesting.
Warm up those wrists, because you’ll be screwing in light bulbs! Just be careful—those bulbs and glass lampshades are delicate! Drop one on a hard surface, and snap—there it goes. That’s right, we’ve added breakable glass to keep you on your toes. Handle with care, folks!
Oh, and here’s a fun little touch: lamps won’t just hang stiffly from the ceiling anymore. Now they’ll sway gently, adding some life to the spaces you’re working on. It’s the little things that make a big difference, right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/628bd824faa7c6045ba1ae5fc243dc683b2aa696.gif[/img]

[b]What’s on TV?[/b]

TVs are getting a glow-up too. For the retro models, you’ll need to adjust the antenna to pick up a signal. And once you’ve got everything hooked up and working, you can kick back and use a remote control to test the setup. Unless, of course, you’ve misplaced the remote—because, well, we all know how sneaky those things can be!

[b]Flawed But Fun[/b]

Not everything in your electrician journey will go as planned—because where’s the fun in that? Some devices might come with a few… quirks. For example, we’ve added a faulty lamp that’ll burn out any bulb you screw into it. Frustrating? Maybe. Realistic? You bet!
And who knows what other surprises we’ve got up our sleeves? Let’s just say we’ve got a few more tricks in the wiring for you.

[b]Stay Tuned[/b]

Excited? You should be! We’re working hard to make sure this game is as electrifying as possible. Keep an eye out for more updates—there’s a lot more current running through Electrician Simulator VR.

notes.title: Detect, Connect, Master!
notes.content:
[h2]Hey there, Electricians! ⚡[/h2]

We bet you’re buzzing with excitement for the VR version of Electrician Simulator, right? Well, we’ve got some shocking updates to share with you today—partly to satisfy your curiosity and partly to amp up your anticipation! Trust us, there’s going to be plenty to spark your interest. Ready to plug into the details? Let’s go!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/49434b865000b6a88a66523ae1729084db7d58df.png[/img]

[b]Big Changes in the Cable Game[/b]

In the VR version, you’ll still be doing the classics: connecting wires in junction boxes, installing switches and sockets, and running cables along walls to power up devices. But here’s the twist—we’ve recharged these mechanics specifically for VR to make them more immersive and hands-on.
The biggest overhaul? Cable detection. Now, instead of automatically knowing where wires are hidden, you’ll need to trace them manually on the wall. Sound tricky? Well, that’s the life of an electrician! Cables don’t just announce themselves—you’ve got to go find them. And to help you out, we’ve added a new tool to your kit:

The Cable Detector – This little beauty lets you locate hidden wires and even measures voltage. Handy, right? Just make sure you’ve got it packed before heading out to your next job!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/81b9318b1ebc80f3b0f70f437b27ee2023c8117e.gif[/img]

And to make things even smoother, we’re introducing the Cable Bundle. This trusty companion will be your go-to for laying down new wiring and getting the job done right.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/cd80da16918fa5c21ee833aeba3b65bde590b408.gif[/img]

[b]Don’t Blow a Fuse[/b]

Fuses are still part of the job, and we’ve recharged their mechanics for VR. But wait—there’s more! To turn up the voltage (pun intended), we’ve added some extra challenges.
Picture this: the lights go out with a loud snap, and you’re stumbling in the dark trying to figure out what went wrong. Sound familiar? Fuses are your circuit’s bodyguards, keeping overloads at bay, and now they’ve got limits. Each fuse can only handle a certain load, depending on the voltage requirements of the devices connected to it. Exceed the limit? Boom—fuse blown.
It’s up to you to wire everything up smartly so the whole system runs like a dream. Think you’re up to the task?

[b]Stay Current[/b]

Feeling energized? We hope so! These are just a few of the updates we’ve got in store, and there’s much more where that came from. We can’t wait for you to dive into the world of VR electrician work—it’s going to be electrifying!
Let us know what you think—your feedback is the spark that keeps us going!

Stay connected with us!
[b]Electrician Simulator VR Dev Team[/b]

notes.title: A spark of change!
notes.content:
[h2]Hi Electricians![/h2]

We are working at high speed, after all, we aim to bring Electrician Simulator to virtual reality. This requires us, first of all, to take a proper look at the whole of the existing game. Electrician Simulator on PC and consoles was of course in 3D, but now we have to make it even more than 3D. All of the existing actions have to be redesigned to align with the specificity of VR. So that you can fully feel like electricians, pick up tools and get down to wiring.

All of the actions, that is, what kind of actions? Will Electrician Simulator become a completely different game through VR? Is there anything old left in it?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/959af004a1ddc40bbe5113c7fa618a07c7da9776.png[/img]

[b]Something old[/b]

Certainly the essentials. Your favorite places remain in the game, but in a completely new version and with new mechanics. You will see familiar houses and familiar tasks. Let us share which ones we've already transferred to VR mechanics. Setting up items such as light switches and junction boxes, connecting plugs and junction box cables to outlets. Installing outlets and switches on the junction box, installing fuses and lamps, also screwing in bulbs. We'll write more about all this in detail in the future, because for practically every one of these things we have some additions planned, whether more stylistic or new, interesting mechanics to diversify the gameplay.

[b]Something new[/b]

Just as various perks will enter the installation assembly, the game as a whole will receive some changes and novelties. One such major change will be the functioning of the store. In previous versions, you could only access the store from your garage, so you had to make all your purchases before going on a work assignment. Now you will have access to it all the time, so even if you forget to get something, it will only take a few clicks, because you always have the store at hand. In addition, if you don't need something, it won't have to dust at your workshop, from now on we have also introduced the possibility to sell items in the store.

[b]Unique mechanics[/b]

Speaking of novelties, we are also introducing unique mechanics in some levels. Such tasks as opening cardboard boxes and even... extinguishing a fire await you! It's getting really hot.

[b]Anything for you[/b]

We are constantly trying to come up with the most interesting solutions and novelties for our loyal players, veterans of the PC or console versions, while still staying true to what Electrician Simulator is. Keep your fingers crossed for us, and we will do our best to meet your requirements and keep you happy!

Let's stay in touch!
[b]Electrician Simulator VR Dev Team[/b]

notes.title: Electrician Simulator VR is coming!
notes.content:
Dear Players!

In September 2022, we released the Electrician Simulator on Steam. The game received free updates for almost a year, with new content and missions. In May 2023, we released DLC extending the game to smart devices, and in autumn 2023, all console owners could play the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312719/1ba442beed2347ade9df682408d39df29a277d7b.png[/img]

[b]It's nice to see you after the break![/b]

Today we are announcing something we have been working hard on for the past months. Encouraged by the extremely warm reception of Electrician Simulator and seeing the potential of this game in another version, we decided to create a new version of the title - this time completely in VR!

[b]Electrician Simulator VR[/b] is the game you know so well, but diversified with redesigned missions, customers now having their own voices, new mechanics, and even more fun gameplay. If you enjoyed the original title, we guarantee that the VR version experience will be even better!

We are also already declaring that the game will receive our full support upon release. We will want to further develop this product with you by releasing free content expansions. In the meantime, we encourage you to add the game to your Wishlist and to join our Discord server.

[b]See you there![/b]
Dorian Loewe
Producer
